page.layout: One page of text, set as verse in italic, without a heading. Running head centred at top. Page number at top right.

p.i: Lugeri vetat: & miseris sine honore sepulchri, Innuidet & matrum lachrymas testemque doloris Atrum habitu, vacuoque nouissima verba sepulcro, Ne dum lugubris passim se ostendit amictus, Victa suos tandem reputans Hispania casus, Forte metu instantis iamiam vasana[?] ruina, Qui sibi tantorum fax est & causa malorum Eripiat vetulo morientia sceptra tyranno. Ille tamen tibi, Christe, minas, totique ferebat Ille gregi, & duris Pontum vincire parabat Compedibus, flavosque iterum, tua regna Britānos. Quid dicam Allobrogas eadem & funesta mo- ventes Arma, per obiectas saxis conatibus undas Terruerisne se subito intercepta doleret Et cadere, & causam exitii praebere Geneua Lausanna, ac traheret magnam hac iactura rui- nam? Sic qui olim iratos iussisti ponere ventos, Et maria, actumidos verbo considere fluctus, Ne sociis, rate demersa, foret unda sepulcrum: Turbine nunc magno ruere, in seseque vicissim Insanire iubes ventos, & surgere fluctus, Hostili ne casa cadant tua pignora fraude. Ecce iterum, dum cuncta fero molimine tentat Guisius, & summa se somniat arce locatum Nec reputat quas sit pro tanto errore daturus Iustitiae poenas, proque his immanibus ausis:

page.notes: Line 6: "vasana" is doubtful (possibly "vastana"). Line 2: "testemque" has an accent-like mark over the e that I read as a printed accent; the reading is doubtful. Line 12 and line 16 end in hyphens at the line break ("mo-", "rui-"), so the continuation words are kept whole with their hyphens. Long s is rendered as s throughout (e.g. "sine", "miseris", "Guisius"). Printed "vv"-ligature "ff" for long ss is read as "ss". No stanza breaks are visible, so the poem is one paragraph.
